fields.v: Jin, H., Lian, D., Wang, X., Xie, H. (2026). MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents. arXiv:2610.38332v1 [cs.LG], 28 Oct 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2610.38332v1 [cs.LG], 28 Oct 2026; marked 'Preprint. Under review.', no published venue
University of Science and Technology of China and State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, Hefei (Jin, Lian, Xie); Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence, Renmin University of China (Wang)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — MUSE memory framework for scientific coding agents, evaluated against ten baselines (Vanilla + nine memory/retrieval methods) on four benchmarks, with ablations and a transfer experiment
MUSE (no version). Baselines: Vanilla agent (no memory), Trajectory RAG, ReasoningBank, ReMe, TRAD, AdaMEM, AutoSci-SciMem, EvoScientist, Agent KB, ACE

Three memory banks built from historical trajectories: L0 GlobalMemBank (consolidated, reviewed cross-task lessons, given in full; advisory budget 80,000 tokens), L1 approach-level lessons (solution outline, tool choices, applicability) with source material, L2 implementation-level lessons (code details, rationale, outcome); indexes of historical submissions and errors; gate review notes. No specification

Memory construction (offline): per-attempt extraction by an agent -> consolidation into L0 (add/replace/retire) -> bank-wide review -> freeze. Solving: initialization with L0 + top-5 problem-matched L1 -> during execution, after designated tool returns (Write, Bash), four-route retrieval of L2/submissions/errors -> LLM gate selects at most one source and writes a review note, or skips -> agent continues to final submission
None (LLM gate and LLM review of the global bank; no human annotation)
Full workflow (memory construction and runtime injection) on four benchmarks, plus ablations
Not classifiable (experience memory / context injection, no specification); authors' terms: 'multi-level memory', 'selective runtime injection'
Mixed: new code from task specification (PDE solvers, GPU kernels) and existing code bases (SWE-bench Science scientific repository repair)
Test tasks: PDEAgent-Bench 451, KernelBenchX 122, KernelGenBench-MS 140, SWE-bench Science 84 (extraction sets 194, 53, 63, 35; about 30% random sample)
Scientific coding: numerical PDE solving (DOLFINx/PETSc), GPU kernel optimization (Triton/PyTorch, CUDA), scientific software repair; Python
N/A (no human participants)
None per configuration; total API expenditure about US$1,500 across preliminary experiments, memory construction and evaluation reported; task wall-clock limits stated
Verifier pass rate (PDE, SWE Science); kernel correctness rate (hidden assessments)
None

Kernel acceleration rate: share of test tasks correct with valid timing and speedup >= 1.01x over reference
Automatic: public benchmarks' verifiers and hidden assessments run after solving (not returned to agent); kernels timed on the same A100 GPU under a lock

Agent ZCode + glm-5.3-flash (high reasoning effort) for all. No success criterion stated by the authors for any configuration (pass/correctness and acceleration are metrics; the 1.01x speedup threshold defines a per-task acceleration hit, not configuration success); cost not reported per configuration. Values PDE pass / KBX correct, accel / KGB correct, accel / SWE Science pass (%): (a) Vanilla (baseline): 44.8 / 57.4, 31.1 / 44.3, 8.6 / 29.8. (b) Trajectory RAG: 72.3 / 53.3, 29.5 / 57.9, 12.1 / 28.6. (c) ReasoningBank: 63.6 / 59.8, 28.7 / 47.9, 15.7 / 31.0. (d) ReMe: 50.1 / 50.0, 29.5 / 40.0, 20.0 / 35.7. (e) TRAD: 75.8 / 60.7, 29.5 / 48.6, 9.3 / 31.0. (f) AdaMEM: 55.7 / 59.0, 32.8 / 47.1, 16.4 / 28.6. (g) AutoSci-SciMem: 78.5 / 63.1, 33.6 / 47.9, 16.4 / 32.1. (h) EvoScientist: 87.8 / 58.2, 29.5 / 50.0, 18.6 / 31.0. (i) Agent KB: 69.6 / 59.8, 27.9 / 50.0, 18.6 / 34.5. (j) ACE: 83.8 / 66.4, 36.9 / 50.7, 17.9 / 31.0. (k) MUSE: 92.2 / 79.5, 44.3 / 66.4, 24.3 / 40.5. All (a)-(k): no criterion stated by the authors. Ablations: MUSE L0 only PDE 82.7; L0+L1 89.4; MUSE w/o gate PDE 90.7, KBX 66.4/37.7, KGB 62.1/20.0, SWE 32.1. Transfer KBX->KGB: MUSE 62.1/25.0, L0 53.6/15.7, L0+L1 54.3/23.6; Agent KB 48.6/17.9; ACE 50.0/22.1. No criterion stated by the authors

Tasks: four public benchmarks; ~30% of problems randomly sampled for memory extraction (one rollout without memory per problem, shared by all memory methods), rest for test. Configurations: 11 (Vanilla + 9 memory/retrieval baselines + MUSE) plus ablations. Baseline: Vanilla agent. Held constant: agent (ZCode), model (glm-5.3-flash), source trajectories (shared rollouts), tool permissions per benchmark, time limits, knowledge budget (80,000 tokens, 'matching the comparison's knowledge budget'); whether baselines use the same embedding model is Not stated. Acceptance tests: hidden benchmark verifiers. Repetitions: Not stated (apparently one run). Human intervention: none
fields.why: The draft listed the embedding model as held constant; the text names Qwen3-Embedding-8B only for MUSE and says baselines share the solving agent and source data. Added the shared knowledge budget stated in the consolidation prompt (p. 13)

fields.v: MUSE best on all six metrics: PDE 92.2 vs EvoScientist 87.8 (Vanilla 44.8); KBX 79.5/44.3 vs ACE 66.4/36.9; KGB 66.4 vs RAG 57.9 and accel 24.3 vs ReMe 20.0; SWE Science 40.5 vs ReMe 35.7 (Vanilla 29.8). No significance tests or variance reported

Separated MUSE from baselines on point estimates; baselines often close to each other and some below Vanilla (e.g. ReMe on KBX/KGB, RAG on SWE Science). Repeatability not addressed (single runs, no variance). Limitations stated: one backbone and agent interface due to cost

Single backbone/agent (ZCode + GLM-5.3-flash) due to evaluation cost; only one transfer direction (KBX -> KGB); frozen banks, no continual memory updates (consolidation, conflict resolution, retirement as environments evolve as future work)

Tables 2, 3, 5 and 6 jumbled by pdftotext; values rebuilt in row order and checked against text (e.g. ACE KBX 66.4/36.9, RAG KGB 57.9, ReMe accel 20.0, PDE 451 and KGB 140 test tasks). Code stated as available (link not in extracted text). All prompts given in Appendix B; environment versions in Appendix A.2. Hardware: 2x AMD EPYC 7742, 8x A100 40GB. No pre-registration. Language: Python (Triton kernels)
